note: The Teutonic Order's Baltic state transformed from a crusading military order-state into a secular duchy when Grand Master Albert of Hohenzollern-Ansbach (1511–1525) converted to Lutheranism on Martin Luther's advice (1525) and secularized the remaining Ducal Prussia as a hereditary Hohenzollern duchy under Polish suzerainty. The transformation was theologically radical — the first major application of Lutheranism to state reorganization — and politically significant: the Hohenzollern Duchy of Prussia became the nucleus of the future Kingdom of Prussia that eventually unified Germany.

_quarry.structural_significance: Albert's conversion and secularization creates Ducal Prussia as the first Protestant state; the Hohenzollern duchy becomes the nucleus of the Prussian state that eventually absorbs Poland and unifies Germany; the secularization is one of the first and most consequential acts of the Reformation
